PullRequest.Title: sessions: manage Automations as a phone-first page
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## What changed

On phones, Automations is now a dedicated page in the mobile entry instead of the desktop catalogue squeezed into the drawer.

- **Automations page:** Lists schedules and recent runs. Tapping a schedule opens an action sheet to run, edit, pause or resume, or delete it. Tapping a recent run opens its conversation.
- **Create and edit:** A full-page form with native pickers and Cancel and Save in the header, selected by the mobile entry. The browser Back gesture closes the form without saving, but is held while a save is in progress so it can't interrupt it. Desktop keeps the existing dialog.
- **Native pickers:** `SelectBoxNative` has a new `nativeActivation` option. When enabled, it ignores the workbench Gesture, so iOS opens its native picker on tap. The option defaults to off, so desktop behavior is unchanged.
- **One presentation per entry:** This follows the same pattern as `ChatViewFactory`. Shared code exposes hooks and registers nothing; each entry registers its own presentation.
  - `AutomationDialogService` is now an abstract base that owns validation and saving. `DefaultAutomationDialogService` (centered dialog with a button bar) and `MobileAutomationDialogService` (full page with Cancel and Save in the header) supply the chrome, focus order and form presentation.
  - The form takes an `IAutomationFormPresentation` hook (prompt label, schedule select factory) instead of a phone flag.
  - New `automations.desktop.contribution.ts` registers the desktop dialog, the cards view, the catalogue editor, their accessible views and **Manage Automations**. `sessions.common.main.ts` imports it. `mobile.contribution.ts` registers the mobile dialog, view and accessible views.
  - Accessibility is split into a desktop cards version, a mobile version, and shared helpers in `automationAccessibleContent.ts`.
  - A new isolation test in `sessionsPresentationDependencies.test.ts` fails if either entry pulls in the other's Automations view, dialog, catalogue editor or accessible view, or registers the dialog service more than once.
- **Polish:** Phone notification rows are 56px tall, schedule chevrons use the codicon size token, and the drawer's collapsible-section chevrons are right-aligned. They inherited a desktop `margin-right` and `letter-spacing` before.
- **Shared state:** `SHOW_DISABLED_AUTOMATIONS_STORAGE_KEY` moved to `automationViewState.ts` so the desktop and phone views share it.

## Why

The phone drawer showed the desktop Automations catalogue: dense rows, hover-only actions, and a modal dialog with custom dropdowns that didn't open on iOS. This follows the mobile direction of a small native-feeling feature set instead of reusing desktop parts.

## Reviewer notes

- `src/vs/base` changes are limited to the opt-in `nativeActivation` flag.
- Known separate issue, not addressed here: after opening a run and going back, the mobile title bar can still show the chat title (`mobileTitlebarPart.ts`).
- This change doesn't overlap with #349979 (Customizations inspector) or #348986 (Automations behind the drawer).

## Testing

- `npm run transpile-client`: passed
- `cd build && node --test lib/test/sessionsPresentationDependencies.test.ts`: **41 passing, 0 failing**
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --runGlob 'vs/sessions/**/*.test.js' --browser chromium`: **8978 passing, 18 pending**
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/test/browser/automationDialog.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/automationsView.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/test/browser/automationsTable.test.ts --browser webkit`: **519 passing**
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in changed files. The only errors are in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/**` because my local `node_modules` has an older `@microsoft/copilot-sdk` than required.
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: the layer import checker passed. The type-check step fails only on the same local SDK mismatch.
- `npm run check-mobile-boundary`: passed (120 reviewed contributions)
- `npm run stylelint`: passed
- Pre-commit hooks (hygiene, oxlint, formatting) passed.
- Manual check:
  - Mobile (iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 26.4, and Playwright WebKit): open the drawer, then Automations. Tap a schedule, then Edit. The full-page form shows Cancel and Save in the header and native selects; Cancel closes it. Change a schedule to Weekly on Wednesday and Save; open a recent run; the drawer chevrons line up.
  - Desktop web (`/agents` without `mobile=1`, Chromium): Automations opens the cards view; choosing a template opens the centered dialog with Cancel and Create in its footer. No registration errors.
  - Loaded modules on `/agents`: desktop requests `automationsEditor.js`, `automationsModalWidget.js` and `automationsModal.css`; the phone entry requests none of them. Neither route reports page errors.

Not tested: persistence for signed-in cloud users and actual scheduled runs.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop and mobile entry startup, including restoring an open Automations page
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Entry modules and BlockRestore registrations must load before restoration. View construction occurs only when the custom view is mounted; a restored page renders cached/provider state without awaiting its background refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load Automations presentation modules and CSS with the selected entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One entry-selected presentation dependency graph; desktop retains its existing cards, catalogue editor, and dialog dependencies, while mobile no longer imports those desktop presentations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both entries transitively imported the desktop view, editor, accessibility presentation, and dialog service through shared contributions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Module loading is on startup's dependency path; removing desktop dependencies reduces the mobile graph.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire an authoritative AutomationCatalog subscription for an agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subscription per connected provider store, not per rendered automation or history row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider-owned subscriptions supplied the desktop presentation mounted on mobile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider state arrives asynchronously; the page can show loading/cached state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Entry dependency graph and number of connected provider stores; no new per-schedule startup instantiation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: BlockRestore contribution registration is synchronous; asynchronous provider loading retains its existing scheduling. No new startup fan-out was identified.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing module cache and provider-owned observable catalogue state are reused. Presentation services remain delayed; custom view ownership releases mounted views when replaced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from entry import diffs, delayed singleton registration, CustomViewService registration, and CustomViewNode ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Bundle byte sizes and actual cold-start duration were not measured; historical provenance does not establish a specific shipped regression fix.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Mobile dependency isolation removes desktop presentation work; desktop registrations are relocated rather than duplicated.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Automations, refresh the catalogue, retry failures, and observe recent-run updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous view rendering shows available state immediately. Automatic refresh is off the navigation critical path; explicit Retry awaits the existing provider refresh to publish updated schedules and history.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh repository capabilities and paginated automation definitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One capability request per distinct remembered/selected/recent repository, followed by definition pages of up to 100 entries for eligible repositories. Repository roots are deduplicated by repositoryKey.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: AutomationsCardsWidget used the identical immediate refresh and 60-second scheduler and the same provider implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background on page entry and the 60-second cadence; completion is necessary to replace cached catalogue data.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List runs for included cloud definitions and fetch details for active tasks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One listRuns request per included definition, returning at most 50 tasks; additional task-detail requests only for active task states. At most four definition workers run concurrently, with task details awaited sequentially inside each worker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same history requests, visibility filtering, four-worker limiter, and active-run polling before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: History publishes after the existing history operation completes; cached state remains usable meanwhile.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve recent workspace roots to repository identities through the existing provider-supplied resolver.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolution per recent workspace root before deduplicating repository API calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same recent-workspace resolution was invoked by the previous cards refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolution precedes that provider's catalogue refresh but does not block initial page mounting.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible schedules N, retained runs R, catalogued sessions S, and distinct cloud repositories G. Session resolution builds maps in O(S+R); history initially displays 10 runs plus active/focused exceptions and grows by pages of 20.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider refresh uses Promise.all across stores. Each cloud store serializes catalogue/history/mutations through its existing Sequencer; repository catalogue requests are sequential, and history uses a four-worker limiter. The scheduler is cancelled while refreshing and disposed with the view; active-cloud history polling remains the existing 15-second cadence.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider catalogue/history snapshots survive failures. Definition refreshes join refreshPromise; history refreshes join historyRefresh. Background refresh preserves target-eligibility caches; foreground Retry clears existing eligibility/failure caches. Cached rendering does not eliminate the intentional refresh requests.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the extracted scheduler's exact before/after match and traced cloud provider/store implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Real catalogue sizes, number of active tasks, and request durations are unknown. No runtime profiling was performed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence new regression. Existing refresh boundaries and limits are preserved. The new mobile row update loop was compared against the previous cards' run-dependent autoruns, which already performed catalogue-wide formatting and DOM updates; a new collection-scaling cost was not established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or edit an automation, choose a template/workspace, save, and dismiss with Cancel or browser Back
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The requested form constructs its prompt editor and controls synchronously. Saving waits for draft synchronization, customization choices, configuration capture, and then the selected provider's authoritative persistence. Browser Back is held only during commit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search repositories and check repository metadata/manageability for a chosen cloud target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Search results are checked in batches of five; target eligibility is keyed by workspace URI and uses a five-slot limiter. A cold private-target check reads metadata and configuration; warm keyed eligibility avoids repeating it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shared renderForm and workspace/provider configuration hooks issued these operations in the former desktop dialog on mobile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Target eligibility must resolve before that target can be saved; these requests occur after the user requests the form or picker.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire a selected-target customization scope and wait for authoritative draft session configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One customization load per changed target key, with prior requests cancelled; one selected draft's configuration capture at Save, or capture while retargeting. Work is not issued per schedule picker option.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical shared form target-key deduplication, synchronization, capture, and scope disposal paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Customization resolution and configuration readiness are prerequisites for persistence.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist a cloud definition using capability preflight and authoritative mutation calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Create performs capability preflight plus one create request; a successful edit performs capability preflight, one authoritative definition get, and one update. Requests concern only the selected automation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same guarded commands and provider methods persisted the former form.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Save remains pending until the mutation finishes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the selected definition change and wait for authoritative host state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected create/update operation after the existing target/configuration work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider route and host-state wait were used by the previous dialog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Commit completion is required before the form closes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Repository search results, selected-target customizations, template count, prompt size, and actual target changes. Three schedule selects are constructed, irrespective of total saved schedule count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Save is guarded by saveInProgress. Draft synchronization runs one loop and coalesces pending target changes. Cloud operations retain their per-store Sequencer; target checks retain their five-slot limiter. Navigation registration uses MutableDisposable and replaces rather than accumulates history handles.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Templates read existing plugin blueprint observables only when requested on mobile; they do not add file reads. Customization loads deduplicate an unchanged serialized target key. Shared draft synchronization preserves per-target configuration. Existing provider eligibility and catalog caches are retained.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from unchanged shared form/capture paths and new surface/button implementations. Gesture.ignoreTarget returns a removable registration owned by each SelectBoxNative.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider resolution durations and prompt/customization sizes were not measured; upstream implementation costs remain pre-existing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Presentation hooks do not increase persistence cardinality or introduce eager form work before it is requested; form resources, window listeners, resize observation, and navigation handles have explicit disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run, pause/resume, cancel a scheduled chat, or delete a selected automation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The mobile action sheet selects one existing guarded command. Confirmation precedes destructive work; command completion waits for the same selected-provider mutation/run dispatch as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Preflight and mutate or dispatch the selected cloud automation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Delete uses capability preflight and one delete. Run uses capability preflight, an authoritative get, and one manual dispatch, followed by existing coalesced history discovery. Enable/disable uses the existing selected-definition update sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Desktop row/card actions used the same commands, provider routing, preflights, dispatch, and history discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Selected action waits for completion; background run discovery proceeds afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request one selected host run, definition change, or history-aware deletion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected automation request; history/session cleanup scales with that selected automation's retained history under the unchanged deletion implementation, not with all rows shown in the mobile action sheet.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same host run/change/delete methods and cleanup semantics.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command waits for existing authoritative response/state handling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected automation, its associated history/session resources for deletion, and explicit user actions; the action sheet does not fan out requests over the catalogue.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cloud requests are serialized through the existing store Sequencer. Host actions retain existing request/state waits. The new scheduled-chat confirmation adds no background or repeated operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Active cloud runs are checked before dispatch. Provider-owned state supplies enablement and management choices. Mutation-uncertain state prevents repeated blind submissions until refresh, unchanged by this PR.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from MobileAutomationsView.manage routing to AutomationCommands and traced unchanged provider mutation methods.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Deletion-history sizes and host/network latency are unknown; no new multiplicity was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Mobile choices expose existing operations rather than adding catalogue-wide boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a recent automation run's conversation and return to Automations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The shared history handler resolves an uncatalogued resource if necessary, then opens one session. SessionsService mounts the conversation before provider preparation/loading completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve an uncatalogued cloud task conversation through the existing task resolver/provider activation and session model resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only the clicked run is resolved. Already catalogued tasks bypass the cloud task-resolution branch; the subsequent SessionsService resolution also uses that existing cached state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The desktop history component on mobile used exactly the same openRunSession handler and session resolver.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resource resolution precedes opening the conversation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider-specific preparation/reconnection and chat loading for the selected session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected session's existing preparation/load work, not all recent runs; an already visible chat can be revealed through its existing opener.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same shared session-open, provider preparation, and readiness path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Conversation UI mounts before preparation finishes, but full session readiness waits for provider loading.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Run/session catalogue size controls in-memory resolution maps; expensive open operations are selected-run scoped. Rendering initially pages history at 10 runs with active/focused exceptions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: SessionsService cancels superseded opens through its existing navigation token. Reopening and provider preparation are awaited together after mounting; no new multi-run concurrency was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Shared SessionsManagementService catalogue avoids uncatalogued-task resolution for warm resources. History session projections are reused and removed when runs/sessions disappear. Replacing the custom view disposes its history groups and refresh scheduler.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from reuse of AutomationHistorySection without an overriding openSession hook and traced SessionsService/provider branches.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific chat fetch/reconnect durations were not measured; these downstream operations are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Recent-run navigation preserves the existing expensive call path and caching behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read Automations with Accessible View and interact with phone notifications/native pickers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessible content is synchronously assembled on request from in-memory schedules, runs, sessions, and chat models. Notification layout updates when phone-layout mode changes. Native select activation is handled by the browser.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Accessible text scales with visible schedules and retained runs; existing run/session matching and chat-progress formatting remain shared. Notification row height changes from 44 to 56 pixels without changing notification count or update frequency. Native schedule controls remain three fixed select widgets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Requested accessibility assembly and notification sizing are synchronous UI work. Notification sizing uses the same layout-policy autorun and reset-on-dispose. No added event-frequency multiplier or forced-layout loop was established.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Accessible views read provider snapshots and storage settings without new network/filesystem calls. Shared accessibility helper extraction preserves previous matching/formatting. Native gesture registrations and listeners are disposed with their controls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the accessibility before/after extraction, notification sizing's unchanged caller, CSS diffs, and Gesture.ignoreTarget disposal implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Accessible-output lengths and device rendering time were not measured. A small extra empty-history helper allocation is insufficient to establish a meaningful regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changes are presentation sizing/activation and shared formatting, without a concrete new expensive boundary or retained-resource lifecycle problem.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base 0089444c17dd066ec8a78e3a941e9f39bb93ec83. Inspected the complete 36-file inventory and all diff pages, traced entry/view ownership, refresh coalescing and repository/history cardinality, form capture/persistence, selected actions, run navigation, native gesture disposal, accessibility, and notification layout. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regressions qualified. No concrete historically attributable regression fix qualified for blame-based learning. Static read-only analysis; no profiling or runtime measurements.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
